messages:
Ruth: FYI — Customer FinInsights on Dedicated (tenant fin-123) is seeing 429s + high tail latency on /v1/generate since ~09:10 UTC. They say it started after rolling workloads with lots of long contexts (~60k-90k tokens). Error in logs: 'KV_CACHE_EVICT_THROTTLE'. Model: redwood-3b-quant-v2 pinned to dc-eu-3 pool. This is P1 for them. Request IDs: req_2024-06-15_09:12:33, req_2024-06-15_09:14:07. Can eng triage? (Customer wants ETA)

Miguel: ACK. Can you paste one of the raw request IDs + the log slice (last 10 lines) and any metric snapshots you have? For now ask customer to temporarily reduce long-context jobs if possible. Pinging @Priya and @eng-oncall.

Ruth: Logs (copied from customer):
```
[09:12:33] req_2024-06-15_09:12:33: worker-7: KV_CACHE_EVICT_THROTTLE tenant=fin-123 model=redwood-3b-quant-v2 ctx_tokens=87234 evictions=412
[09:12:33] req_2024-06-15_09:12:33: worker-7: emit 429 tenant=fin-123 reason=kv_throttle
[09:14:07] req_2024-06-15_09:14:07: worker-9: KV_CACHE_EVICT_THROTTLE tenant=fin-123 ctx_tokens=65890 evictions=298
```
Also attached a small repro script they used to hit generate with long context (they can halt it on request).

Miguel: Running quick internal metrics for pool dc-eu-3 and tenant fin-123 (via infractl):
```
> infractl metrics query --pool dc-eu-3 --tenant fin-123 --range 1h --metrics kv_evictions_per_minute,kv_fragmentation_ratio,worker_free_kv_mem
kv_evictions_per_minute: baseline=12 -> spike=185 at 09:11
kv_fragmentation_ratio: 0.68 (high)
worker_free_kv_mem (avg): 150MB -> min=42MB
worker_restarts: 2 in last 30m (OOM margin restarts)
```
Conclusion: KV pressure + fragmentation causing frequent evictions and guardrail throttles. Looks correlated with long-context requests.

Priya: Checked autoscale for the pool. Policy shows min_shards=4 max_shards=12, but last scale action had backoff due to recent surge and cooldown of 30m; current active_shards=5. Also found a policy hiccup: burst_autoscale disabled for this tenant (likely from an older org config).
```
> infractl pool get dc-eu-3
active_shards: 5
last_scale_time: 2024-06-15T08:48:30Z
burst_autoscale: disabled for tenant fin-123
```
Short-term mitigations:
- Ask CS to pause/slow long-context ingestion for FinInsights (done?)
- Temporarily increase kv_cache_high_watermark for redwood-3b-quant-v2 on dc-eu-3 (raise from 0.7 -> 0.85) to reduce evictions. Will need rolling restart of workers.
- Manually scale pool +1 shard to give breathing room (no config change).
Longer-term: re-enable burst_autoscale for tenant and investigate fragmentation root cause (maybe noisy neighbor long churn).

Sasha: I've messaged the customer asking them to throttle their repro and provided an ETA window. They're willing to pause non-prod workload for 45 min. I'll keep them updated.

eng-oncall: I'm spinning +1 shard in dc-eu-3 now as emergency mitigation. Also queuing a rolling restart of workers that will pick up new kv_cache_high_watermark. Creating ticket RED-4237 and setting priority=P1. Steps I'm taking:
1) infractl pool scale --pool dc-eu-3 --delta +1 --reason "emergency kv pressure"
2) infractl config apply --pool dc-eu-3 --model redwood-3b-quant-v2 --set kv_cache_high_watermark=0.85
3) rolling restart workers (1 at a time) to pick config

Miguel: Note — rolling restart will temporarily increase latency for in-flight long-context requests; coordinate with CS if they need a maintenance window. Also schedule a post-mortem to look at defragmentation heuristics; fragmentation ratio >0.6 repeatedly is a smell.

Ruth: Customer agreed to pause their long-context test. Sasha to confirm when it's paused. eng-oncall, please post exact timestamps for scale/restart so I can tell the customer.

eng-oncall: Scale request submitted at 2024-06-15T09:20:05Z. Rolling restart start 2024-06-15T09:25:00Z, expected finish ~09:40Z. Will update when done. :thumbsup:

Miguel: After scaling + config change we should monitor kv_evictions_per_minute and 429 rate for the tenant for 30m. If still high, next step is to move tenant to an isolated shard pool or require explicit capacity reservation.

Ruth: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket with timeline and customer notes. We'll follow up in RED-4237.
